XVII.}}</noinclude>vvo to him by vvhom they come. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=2}}† It is more profitable for him, if a mil-stone be put about his necke, and he be cast into the sea, then that he scandalize one of these litle ones. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=3}}† Looke vvel to your selues, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 18, 21.''}}* If thy brother sinne against thee, rebuke him: and if he doe penance, forgiue him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=4}}† And if he sinne against thee seuen times in a day, and seuen times in a day be conuerted vnto thee, saying, It repenteth me, forgiue him.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=5}}† And the Apostles said to our Lord, Increase faith in vs. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=6}}† And our lord said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 17, 20.''}}* If you had faith like to a mustard seede, you might say to this mulberie tree, be thou rooted vp, and be transplanted into the sea: and it vvould obey you. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=7}}† And vvhich of you hauing a seruant plovving or keeping cattle, that vvil say to him returning out of the field, Passe quickly, sit downe: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=8}}† and saith not to him, Make ready supper, and gird thy self, and serue me vvhiles I eate and drinke, and afterward thou shalt eate and drinke? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=9}}† Doth he giue that seruant thankes, for doing the things vvhich he commaunded him? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=10}}† I trovv not. So you also, vvhen you shal haue done al things that are commaunded you, say, VVe are {{sup|‖}} vnprofitable seruants: vve haue done that vvhich vve ought to doe.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=11}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ THE fourth part of this Gospel, The comming of Christ into Iewrie, towardes his Passion.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 13 Sunday after Pentecost.}}And it came to passe, as he vvent vnto Hierusalem, he passed through the middes of Samaria and Galilee. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=12}}† And vvhen he entred into a certaine tovvne, there mette him ten men that vvere lepers, vvho stoode a farre of: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=13}}† and they lifted vp their voice, saying, {{sc|Iesvs}} maister, haue mercie on vs. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=14}}† Whom as he savv, he said, Goe, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 14, 2.''}}* shevv your selues {{sup|‖}} to the Priests. And it came to passe, {{sup|‖}} as they vvent, they vvere made cleane. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=15}}† And one of them as he savv that he vvas made cleane: vvent backe vvith a loud voice magnifying God, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=16}}† and he fel on his face before his feete, giuing thankes: and this vvas a Samaritane. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=17}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering said, VVere not ten made cleane? and vvhere are the nine? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=18}}† There vvas not found that returned, and gaue glorie to God, but this stranger. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=19}}† And he said to him, Arise, goe thy vvaies: because {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ And yet we see here it was not only faith, but also his thankfulnes & returning to giue glorie to God.}}∷ thy faith hath made thee safe.⊣

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=20}}† And being asked of the Pharisees, VVhen commeth the kingdom of God? he ansvvered them and said, The kingdom of<noinclude>{{rh|||God}}</noinclude>
